name: wall_jump_wheel_wall_exit_pays_nothing_DEFECT
description: DEFECT, current behaviour: The blue car sits on the side wall x = 4096 (rolled 90 degrees, centre 17 uu off the wall, at z 500; it slides slowly down the wall and stays on it) and jumps at decision step 2, leaving the wall at frame 3 with about 390 uu/s away from it. The ball floats at (3400, 0, 500). Hand calc: on frame 3 the car is near (4055, 0, 487) and the ball near (3400, 0, 487), 655 uu apart, so the latch opens with Phi = exp(-655/1410) = 0.6285 and the step pays gamma * Phi = 0.627 at once (about +37.6 at weight 60). Nothing is paid on frames 1-2 (still on the wall). After the exit the car falls away from the wall and lands; landing refunds the approach, so over the whole run the sum is only the small discount leak. The ball has a 1 uu/s upward velocity on purpose (a ball set with exactly zero velocity in the air floats: see tools/reward_lab/README.md). BUT in the engine the car rides the wall on its wheels and `worldContact.hasContact` (a body-collision flag, cleared every tick) stays false, so `OnWall()` is false, the latch never opens, and the exit pays NOTHING. Measured: resting on the wall for 20 steps reports isOnGround true and hasContact false every step; driving up the side wall at 25 degrees reports OnWall on 1 step of 40 (a ramp bump at z 128) and a jump sweep over steps 12-25 never paid. These expectations pin the current (inert) behaviour; the intended ones are in packs/wall_jump_intended.

expect.intent: DEFECT: leaving a wall by the wheels 655 uu from the ball pays 0 because OnWall() needs a body-contact flag the wheels never set (intended: +0.627 on the exit step)
